name: Gandalf
text: The bazaar awakens with ten stalls open and no departures. No Family hand has shuttered a door overnight, and the graveyard holds no fresh names. I ask Sherlock: which merchant’s silence today troubles you most, given the roster’s stillness?

name: Gandalf
text: I find the ledger still empty and the graveyard silent, yet the merchants’ questions pile up like unclaimed parcels. Sherlock, you have been asked six times about silence; your answers will shape which ledger line we read next. Inigo’s point stands: the only silence that matters is the Family’s absence, and it speaks plainly. I ask Sherlock: when you next answer, will you cite a merchant’s words that do not match the roster’s stillness—or will you name the merchant whose single sentence would break the ledger’s calm?
